scientificAndVisualFindings.visibleChemistry: Three linked generic sugar units, a three-tail fat symbol, a folded bead-chain protein symbol and positive/negative mineral-ion icons are differentiated correctly as broad groups. Food arrows refer to a food mixture, not a claim that a depicted food contains only one constituent.
scientificAndVisualFindings.abstraction: These are class icons rather than literal atom/valence or salt-formula drawings. The fat symbol has three fatty-acid tails and is not a one- or two-tail phospholipid formula. The three ion symbols do not specify a stoichiometric salt unit.
scientificAndVisualFindings.goalRelation: Supports comparing broad submicroscopic structural motifs and mineral micronutrient versus major organic nutrient classes. Vitamin examples, particular formulas and every physiological function remain teaching/task content; the image alone is not a full-goal assessment.
scientificAndVisualFindings.readability: At 360 px all four groups, labels and distinct motifs are recognizable; at 680 px chain/tail/ion details are clear. No essential tiny paragraph text.
scientificAndVisualFindings.oldDelta: The bound current goal has no primary resource; this reviewed existing PNG adds an available image without a new chemical body.
scientificAndVisualFindings.perspective: Front-facing food and class icons; no person/tool/paper viewpoint contradiction.

scientificAndVisualFindings.visibleChemistry: Actual old JPG contains G-T and A-C pairings. The existing PNG shows A-T, G-C, T-A and C-G; the nucleotide icon connects phosphate to sugar to base and the ladder has repeating sugar/phosphate sides plus an information symbol.
scientificAndVisualFindings.abstraction: It is explicitly a schematic Baustein/ladder model: base polygons are not heterocyclic atom formulas, and the repeated two dotted connector rows per pair are generic pairing connectors, not a quantitative hydrogen-bond model. In particular the picture must not be used to teach two hydrogen bonds for G-C: actual Watson-Crick A-T has two and G-C three. No such count claim or atom assignment appears in the supplied image/alt text.
scientificAndVisualFindings.goalRelation: Supports basic nucleic-acid structure and information function. It is a DNA example of the nucleic-acid class, not a depiction of all RNA forms, antiparallel end chemistry or all comparisons with fats/proteins/carbohydrates. Those whole-goal teaching/assessment duties remain separate.
scientificAndVisualFindings.readability: All four base-letter pairs, DNA label, nucleotide group and information cue remain distinct at 360 px; the small Zucker word is supporting detail. At 680 px even supporting wording is legible.
scientificAndVisualFindings.oldDelta: Reuses an already generated correction PNG for the evidenced wrong-base-pair problem. No fresh generation or mandatory cosmetic redesign.
scientificAndVisualFindings.perspective: Flat explanatory ladder, not a literal helix or an atom model. The information-book label faces the viewer and is not reversed relative to a person.

Die lernende Person kann Nahrungsbestandteile als hydrophil, lipophil oder amphiphil einordnen und damit Vitaminresorption, Verweildauer im Körper sowie geeignete Lösemittel bei der Lebensmittelzubereitung begründen.

scientificAndVisualFindings.visibleChemistry: Hydrophilic blue and lipophilic orange examples are separated; amphiphile blue heads face the aqueous blue region and orange tails face the oil region. The circular aggregate has water-facing heads and inward unpolar tails. The intestine label explicitly says Dünndarm, not stomach.
scientificAndVisualFindings.abstraction: Schematic phase and aggregate cartoons, no individual molecule formula, atom count or detailed membrane-transport mechanism. The enlargement illustrates a micellar lumen environment; it does not show intact micelles traversing intestinal epithelium or replacing all vitamin-specific uptake routes.
scientificAndVisualFindings.goalRelation: Supports polarity, phase compatibility and a micellar intestinal-resorption example. It makes no blanket water-soluble=no-storage claim. Water-soluble B12 is a relevant counterexample: substantial body storage and intrinsic-factor-dependent distal-ileal uptake mean polarity alone cannot determine residence time or resorption mechanism. Solvent choice, individual vitamin transport and residence-time limits remain part of the whole goal/profile, not newly waived.
scientificAndVisualFindings.readability: The three class labels, phase orientation, inward micelle tails and Dünndarm remain recognizable at 360 px, with ample contrast and no essential fine text; 680 px is clear throughout.
scientificAndVisualFindings.oldDelta: The actual old JPG places a bile/micelle label with a stomach drawing and groups B vitamins with short-storage wording. The new existing PNG uses a Dünndarm model and removes that universal storage statement.
scientificAndVisualFindings.perspective: No student/paper viewpoint. The magnification link is conventional schematic anatomy rather than a claim of histological scale or direct whole-micelle blood entry.
